title: Arcade drive math
summary: forward + turn and forward - turn, and why it turns.

say.never: In **arcade drive** you steer with two jobs, both on the **left stick**. Up and down says *how fast to go forward or back*. Left and right says *how much to turn*. It feels like driving a car, which is why many drivers like it.

steps.title: In your lesson: Two sticks, two jobs

say.never: In **arcade drive** you steer with two jobs, both on the **left stick**. Up and down says *how fast to go forward or back*. Left and right says *how much to turn*. It feels like driving a car, which is why many drivers like it.
say.bit: Arcade drive: the left stick goes forward and back and also turns. Most drivers prefer it.

marks.label: left and right: no minus sign

say.never: Here's the trick. To turn right, the left wheels must go faster than the right wheels, so the robot curves around to the right. To turn left, it's the other way round. Your code starts from the forward speed and nudges the two sides in opposite directions. Try it with numbers on the next step.
say.bit: To curve right the left side speeds up and the right side slows down; to curve left, the reverse. Start from forward speed and nudge the sides oppositely.

board.code:
turning right:   left side FASTER, right side SLOWER
turning left:    left side SLOWER, right side FASTER
spinning:        sides go OPPOSITE ways

marks.label: wheels on the outside of a turn speed up

say.never: Here's the trick. To turn right, the left wheels must go faster than the right wheels, so the robot curves around to the right. Adding `turn` to one side and subtracting it from the other does exactly that. Try it with numbers on the next step.
say.bit: To turn right, the left side goes faster than the right. Adding and subtracting `turn` does exactly that.

say.never: Work these out in your head before you ever drive. Read each line as: *if the sticks say this, the wheels get that.* Notice that when `forward` is 0, the two sides get opposite numbers, so one pushes and one pulls and the robot spins in place.
say.bit: Work these out in your head before you drive.

board.code:
forward 0.5, turn 0.0  ->  left 0.5,  right 0.5   (straight)
forward 0.0, turn 0.5  ->  left 0.5,  right -0.5  (spin right)
forward 0.5, turn 0.5  ->  left 1.0,  right 0.0   (curve right)

say.never: A **duty cycle** is just *how hard the motor is pushed*. It's a number from **-1.0** (full speed backward) through **0** (stopped) to **1.0** (full speed forward). If your math says 1.5, the motor still only gives 1.0. It can't go past full.
say.bit: A **duty cycle** is how much battery voltage the motor gets, from -1.0 (full reverse) to 1.0 (full forward). Bigger numbers get clipped to 1.0.
